about.title: Capitola Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Capitola draws visitors and locals alike to its village shops, Esplanade restaurants, and beach access points, which means a lot of foot traffic moving across surfaces that aren't always maintained the way they should be. A fall on a wet tile floor, a cracked sidewalk near Bay Avenue, or a poorly marked step at a rental property can lead to real injuries and real medical bills. California law asks whether the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it. That's why what happens in the hours after a fall matters: photos of the spot, names of witnesses, and a request that surveillance footage be preserved can all shape whether a claim holds up. If you were hurt in a fall anywhere in Capitola, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who handles these cases on a contingency basis, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Fall Victims in Capitola Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Capitola businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of footage can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're partly responsible for not seeing a hazard, California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help make sure a fair share of fault is assigned.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Capitola?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If your fall happened on public property, such as a city sidewalk or park, the deadline is much shorter and involves an early claim filing requirement. It's worth talking to an attorney soon after the incident so no deadline gets missed.

items.question: What should I do right after falling at a Capitola business or rental?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of the exact spot, including what caused the fall, and note the date and time. Ask an employee or manager to document the incident and, if possible, request that any surveillance video be preserved before it's automatically deleted. Getting medical care promptly also creates a record connecting your injury to the fall.

items.question: Does it matter if the fall happened on a beach access path instead of inside a store?
items.answer: It can. Outdoor areas like beach walkways, parking lots on 41st Avenue, or exterior stairs are still subject to premises liability rules, but ownership and maintenance responsibility can be more complicated between private and public parties. An attorney can help sort out who was responsible for the specific area where you fell.
